claim: The four network types are defined by how many organizing frames reach the blend. Primary source (Fauconnier and Turner 2003): simplex = one input is a frame, the other holds specific elements; mirror = one organizing frame shared by all spaces; single-scope = different input frames, blend inherits only one; double-scope = essential frame and identity properties from both inputs. They are prototypes on a continuum. The 1998 paper uses older names (frame, one-sided, two-sided networks); the four names come from the 2002 book and later. The 2002 book chapter was not opened.
agent_test: Have the agent label each planned cross-frame step with a type; check label agreement across two runs and a code check that matches the label to which frames' roles are used.

claim: No study found varies Fauconnier and Turner network type and measures an outcome in humans or LLMs. The ACL 2026 position poster by Xi, Cheng, Soni and Turner proposes a rubric but labels no types and reports no scores; Birdsell (2019) is a qualitative n=25 study; Palamas (2025) varies Synectics analogy distance (a different typology). 'Double-scope for novel ideas' is an untested design hypothesis whose only support is the authors' own argument (F&T 1998, 2003).
agent_test: A/B at equal tokens: force single-scope vs double-scope prompts on the same novel-idea tasks; blind-judge novelty and validity.

claim: Human integration cost rises with mapping demand: N400 is smallest for literal, intermediate for literal-mapping, largest for metaphor (linear trend accounts for over 98% of sentence-type variance, N=18), replicated in graded form in later ERP work. Rival theories (structure mapping, career of metaphor, relevance theory) predict the same pattern, so it does not support blending over them.
agent_test: Count error rate per step for same-frame vs cross-frame steps in agent traces; require a check stage after cross-frame steps.

claim: Prior domain knowledge lowers integration cost for novel metaphors (smaller N400 in engineers for engineering metaphors), but the three-way interaction was not significant, so the moderator is weak. PopBlends scene relatedness (product 89.1% vs pop culture 75.9%) hints at the same thin-frame effect.
agent_test: Compare blend quality when frame facts are supplied first vs not, for a thin frame.

claim: LLMs are worse at blending than at association or analogy; the bottleneck is finding a valid shared abstraction (generic space), not building the blend: 43.4% valid blends vs 53.4% analogy vs 59.0% association over 35 LLMs, but 97.1% coherent blends given a valid generic space. Humans are lower on all (12.8% blend). Re-opened and confirmed. Note: Kombine's single-scope/double-scope scale is its own (single-scope = both inputs contribute; double-scope = both fill a shared slot) and is not the 2003 typology. No code-side shared-slot gate has been tested by anyone (gap search). Humans: 120 recruited, N=75 kept. Per-model integration-quality percent is published but not the Q=1/2/3 split; one temperature (0.9) only.
agent_test: Insert a code-side check that the proposed shared slot holds for both inputs before building the blend; measure valid-blend rate with and without the gate.

claim: An LLM proposes bridge concepts with about 56-59% precision per item but at least one good option in five 90-97% of the time; a bridge-concept step more than doubled idea output in a small user study (2.03 vs 0.87 ideas per pair, N=10). Generated attributes are often invented (catchphrases 35% accurate). Re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Generate 5 bridge candidates, filter by check, compare with top-1 choice at equal tokens.

claim: A staged blend scaffold beats a single strong prompt in image-domain studies: stating inputs, how they combine and the implication (IEI) lifted Midjourney win rate 0.26 to 0.35 without longer prompts (length p=0.404); a schema-extract, transfer, diagnose, backtrack loop beat a one-shot blending-theory prompt in a 100-person study (full 4.47/4.56/4.51/4.74/4.76 vs strong prompt 3.97/3.69/3.77/3.89/4.09). Both use author-designed metrics on image tasks.
agent_test: Text-only: require fields inputs / how combined / implications and a critic with backtrack vs one-shot blend prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Models decode blends better than average people but below experts (implication win rate GPT-4o 73.5 vs experts 78.3 vs average people 51.0), with the implication step weakest; judge is GPT-4o with 81-85% agreement to experts.
agent_test: Spend more checking effort on implication claims of a blend than on the identification of inputs.

claim: Input order or weighting changes blends: three of four diffusion blending methods are order-sensitive, no method wins everywhere, and equal weighting (ratio 0.5) maximises blended depiction (BCD 0.621, MCD 0.862); heavy weight on one input collapses toward one concept.
agent_test: Run a blend in both orderings and keep the one that passes a check; log which frame dominated.

claim: Fusion vs replacement mashups: re-reading Figure 5 of Peng et al. shows fusion precision above replacement for 9 of 11 models and for average people (replacement higher only for Claude-3.5-Sonnet and LLaVA-1.6-13B), matching the text. The Figure 5 caption is a wording error. No significance test is given. Balanced two-input blends are easier to decode than one-input-dominant ones.
agent_test: Check blends in both directions: if one input dominates the output (replacement-like), flag it as hard for a reader to decode and ask for the shared structure to be stated.

claim: LLMs produce homogeneous blends: one in five of 2,070 invented concepts repeats a property another model invented; blends are reused 14 times more than analogies; same-provider 2.3 times more than cross-provider. Default model blends are familiar pairs; pushing to less available pairs raised judged novelty (85% of higher-temperature combinations had a new concept; figure not re-opened). Alien Recombination (Hernandez 2024): raising temperature gives combinations new to artworks (85% above temperature 1) but at temperature 3 more than half were still not cognitively unavailable to artists; ranking by cognitive unavailability worked better. GPT-4o also defaults to shallow merges (separate sub-dishes joined at the end; self-BLEU-2 0.929).
agent_test: Sample N blends from one model and count duplicates; compare with a forced far-pair step.

claim: Blending distant domains risks fluent but ungrounded output (hallucination); this is argued in position papers without measurement.
agent_test: Check blend claims against held-out facts; compare ungrounded-claim rate for near vs far frame pairs.

claim: Blending theory is criticised as post hoc and untestable (Gibbs 2000; Ritchie 2004: simpler integration explains many blends). Defenders accept analysis must move past post hoc.
agent_test: Treat the typology as a labeling heuristic; ablate the label and see whether outcomes change.

claim: Even interactive LLM blending tools give imperfect output: Misty mean satisfaction 3.2/5 over 103 operations, 31 below 3; only 5 of 14 (35%) agreed it expressed intent. A reviewable diff with per-part accept helps. Re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Show the projected parts of each input per blend and accept/reject by check; measure retry rate.

claim: Computational and formal blending (Sapper, COINVENT, HETS topological group) shows blends can be run with explicit constraint scoring or proofs where domains are formal; no benchmark exists and Eppe et al. 2018 was opened: it states it has no empirical evaluation and offers value(c) = info + compression - imbalance if consistent. Lieto and Pozzato (arXiv 1811.02366) gives worked examples only. No numbers exist to use as a baseline.
agent_test: For math tasks, require a blend to be checked by computation or proof.

claim: Moving the combine step out of the model into explicit code raised judged novelty in text: Dish COVER (LLM parses and writes; tree edit-distance code blends two recipe trees, filters value, ranks novelty) beat a prompt-tuned GPT-4o. Novelty 3.53 vs 3.146 (p=0.0009, 10 dish pairs) and 3.612 vs 3.141 (p=9.2e-8, 100 recipes each); value about equal in Exp 1 (4.320 vs 4.326) but lower in Exp 2 (85% vs 98% valuable). 48 Prolific raters, Krippendorff alpha about 0.2. Cooking only; baseline was a single call.
agent_test: Text reasoning task: let the model list two frames' parts, have code or a fixed template recombine them, then a validity check; compare with one-shot at equal tokens using blind judges.

claim: By default GPT-4o juxtaposes instead of integrating: for two dishes it prepares each separately and joins them at the end. Evidence is qualitative plus homogeneity numbers (self-BLEU-2 0.929 and 0.912; same-pair cosine 0.90). Kombine names the same failure a concatenation (u and v lines that never share a slot).
agent_test: Reject any blend whose parts can be split back into input A and input B with nothing lost; require one element that uses both frames.

claim: A pre-answer generation step helps text-only reasoning, but the tested step is analogy recall, not blending: analogical prompting gave +4% average accuracy over 0-shot and few-shot CoT (GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces, BIG-Bench; GPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM2), better with larger models. Not equal tokens. No text-only reasoning test of a 'how the inputs combine' step exists (searches this session found none).
agent_test: Add a field 'how the two frames combine' before the answer on a text reasoning set; compare with analogical recall and plain CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Distance between frames trades creativity against coherence in LLM metaphors: with GPT-4 and four Synectics types, Fantasy scored creativity 4.8 and coherence 3.8, Direct scored coherence 4.5 and novelty 3.9 (1,000 AI vs 1,000 human metaphors). Judged by GPT-4 and TF-IDF only; preliminary; not the Fauconnier and Turner types.
agent_test: Make the frame distance a labeled choice and spend more checking after the far choice.

claim: Double-scope blending is double-edged by the founders' own account: two-sided (double-scope) networks have more chance of non-optimal blends and of clashing optimality principles, and also the opportunity for creativity; the main worked case is complex numbers. Argued from after-the-fact cases, no comparison group.
agent_test: After any cross-frame step, run a check that every borrowed role still holds in the target frame.

claim: A code-side score exists for ranking blends but is unvalidated: Eppe et al. (2018) score = information kept + compression - imbalance (half the difference between the two inputs' contribution), zero if inconsistent. The paper says it has no empirical evaluation. The imbalance term is a rough proxy for whether both frames contribute.
agent_test: Implement the score on the agent's own blend candidates and test whether it predicts blind-judge preference.

claim: Ranking candidate far pairs by how unlikely the pair is under a model of existing use beats raising temperature for finding unavailable combinations (Hernandez 2024: art domain, GPT-2 models, 50 inputs x 150 outputs per temperature; at temperature 3 over half still had no unavailable concept). Judged by GPT-4 and image embeddings, no human raters.
agent_test: In a far-pair step, sample many candidate frame pairs, rank by low co-occurrence plus a coherence gate, instead of raising temperature.

claim: Human studies tying network type to novelty or quality of real products do not exist in what was found: Birdsell (2019) had 34 students, 25 usable drawings, five analysed qualitatively, and no type coding. Dreyfus 2014, Turner 2014 and the physics-education work were not opened in the gap search.
agent_test: Not testable from literature; run our own coding of agent outputs by type and blind novelty ratings.
